sections.h2: Hiring an installer, not buying a kit
body: When you search for epoxy garage floor installers, you are really choosing who will prepare your slab, because preparation decides whether the floor lasts. Our crews are our own, not subcontracted, and the crew lead who measures your garage and tests the concrete is on site during the install.

This page focuses on hiring and install day. For a deeper explanation of the layers themselves, including grinding, moisture testing, and why polyaspartic tops an epoxy basecoat, read our page on the garage floor epoxy coating system.

sections.h2: What to ask before you sign
body: Garage floor quotes can be wildly different, and the gap is almost always the system, not the labor rate. One thin layer rolled onto acid-washed concrete and a multi-coat system over a diamond-ground slab are simply not the same floor, even if both are called epoxy. Ask every installer the same questions so you can compare fairly:

Also ask who will actually be on your floor. Some outfits sell the job and hand it to whichever crew is free that week. With us, the person who tested your slab is accountable for the result, and the proposal names every coat so nothing gets quietly downgraded on install day.
bullets: Will the slab be diamond ground or acid etched?
Will you test for moisture, and what happens if it reads high?
What is the basecoat, how thick, and what is the topcoat?
Is the flake a full broadcast or a light scatter?
How are cracks, spalls, and control joints handled?
What does the written warranty cover?

body: A standard residential garage is typically a two-day install. Before we arrive, clear the floor, including shelving that sits on the slab, and plan to park outside for a few days.

Day one is grinding and repair. Crews diamond grind the slab with vacuum dust collection, hand-grind edges and corners, fill cracks and pits, and vacuum thoroughly. The basecoat goes down and flake is broadcast into it while it is wet. Day two starts with scraping off loose flake and vacuuming, then the clear topcoat is applied. Doors stay closed or partly open for ventilation depending on the product and weather.

Light foot traffic is usually fine the following morning. Vehicles wait until the manufacturer's stated cure time has passed, which we confirm with you at the end of day two. Summer heat speeds curing; cool, damp days slow it, so we watch conditions and give you a real date rather than a guess.

Most of our installs are home garages, but the same approach works for detached workshops, hobby barns, golf cart garages, small showrooms, and light-commercial back rooms. Commercial spaces can be scheduled around business hours, including nights and weekends, so the floor is closed for as little operating time as possible.

For businesses, we can provide a certificate of insurance naming your company before mobilization. If your building also needs walls painted, the floor can be coordinated with our warehouse and industrial painting crews or our commercial interior painting team so trades are not stacked on top of each other.

A good share of our calls are floors that are already peeling, usually a kit or a thin coat over an etched slab. The old coating has to be ground off completely before a new system goes down, because new material bonded to failing material just fails together. Our article on fixing peeling garage epoxy explains the warning signs and what removal involves.
Stains from oil and tire marks on bare concrete are also ground out during prep, so an older, well-used slab can still end up looking new once coated.

sections.h2: Getting a quote in North Central Florida
body: Estimates are free. A crew lead visits, measures the floor, notes cracks and stains, and checks moisture. You receive a written, itemized proposal, usually within one business day of the walkthrough, listing the prep, each coat, flake, edge details, and the schedule. Most projects start one to three weeks after approval.

Our crews install floors throughout Alachua, Marion, Levy, Columbia, and Gilchrist counties, most often in and around Gainesville and Ocala. Floors are one of several specialty services we offer alongside standard painting, so if you are also planning to repaint the garage walls or refinish the garage door, it can all go on one schedule.

faqs.q: How long does an epoxy garage floor install take?
faqs.a: A standard residential garage usually takes two working days: grinding, repair, basecoat, and flake on day one, then scraping and topcoat on day two. Large or damaged floors can take longer.

faqs.q: When can I drive on the floor?
faqs.a: Foot traffic is usually fine the next morning. Vehicles wait for the manufacturer's stated cure time, which depends on temperature and humidity. We confirm the date with you before we leave.

faqs.q: Do I need to empty the garage?
faqs.a: Yes. The full floor needs to be clear for grinding and coating, including anything stored along the walls on the slab.

faqs.q: Do you install in commercial spaces?
faqs.a: Yes, including workshops, showrooms, and light-commercial floors. Work can be scheduled outside operating hours, and certificates of insurance are available.
